conviction_note: My findings sum to +2.3 and I am emitting +1.4, because this name's own reaction function has veto power and it is loud: on 2026-03-24 ABC arbitrage disclosed an activity pace 40% above its 2025 monthly average AND fell 8.19%, because reported revenue only matched Kepler Cheuvreux's pessimistic EUR60m case while net income (EUR25.1m) and EPS (EUR0.42) came in under Kepler's EUR27.8m / EUR0.47; and on 2025-09-23 net income doubled with a 20.3% ROE and the stock still fell 1.51% on a weaker H2 pace comment. The three September prints in the baseline moved -0.51%, +1.80% and -1.51%, all inside 2%, so the name's own distribution caps this well below France's 4.19% median. The positive sign survives because the H1 number will be a record half (PAC near EUR50m against EUR36.5m), because the two covering analysts have not revised a price target since 2026-03-24, and because the stock at EUR5.25 sits nearer its EUR4.87 52-week low than its EUR6.19 high with a +1.74% 20-day run-up, i.e. nothing is positioned for it. print_vs_bar is far larger than expected_move precisely because the fundamental beat is close to arithmetic while the reaction is not.
bar: FY2026 consensus of EUR69.75m revenue, EUR31.18m net income and EUR0.52 EPS, polled from the 2 covering analysts (Kepler Cheuvreux, TP ICAP Midcap) by S&P Global, with price targets explicitly 'last updated on Mar 24, 2026' — https://stockanalysis.com/quote/epa/ABCA/forecast/ . There is no published H1-specific consensus for this name; I size the H1 print against the H1 share implied by that unrevised full-year bar (~EUR38m PAC / ~EUR17m net income on a front-loaded split). Cross-checked against the broker numbers reported in French for the last print (Kepler FY2025: EUR60m pessimistic / EUR66m optimistic revenue, EUR27.8m net income, EUR0.47 EPS) — https://www.tradingsat.com/abc-arbitrage-FR0004040608/actualites/abc-arbitrage-malgre-son-allie-donald-trump-et-la-forte-volatilite-des-marches-abc-arbitrage-laisse-les-investisseurs-sur-leur-faim-1159162.html
session_check: bmo, settled three ways rather than taken from the vendor flag. (1) The issuer's own 2026 calendar release states 'The press releases will be published on the dates at 07:00am, before the markets open' — https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/10/31/3178543/0/en/ABC-arbitrage-calendar-of-financial-events-for-the-year-2026.html (2025-10-31). (2) The AMF regulated-information flux timestamps last year's equivalent release, 'ABC arbitrage : Resultat consolide S1 2025', at 2025-09-23T05:00:00+00:00 = 07:00 CEST, i.e. two hours before the 09:00 Paris open — https://www.info-financiere.gouv.fr/api/explore/v2.1/catalog/datasets/flux-amf-new-prod/records?where=identificationsociete_iso_cd_isi%3D%27FR0004040608%27 . (3) The 1 June 2026 trading update PDF carries the header 'Paris, le 1 juin 2026 - 8h00'. Window is close 2026-09-21 -> close 2026-09-22, as the baseline has it.
positioning_check: No disclosed net short position. The AMF 'positions courtes nettes' register was read successfully for this run as of 2026-09-17 (74 French issuers carry an open disclosed position) and does NOT name ABC arbitrage — https://www.data.gouv.fr/api/1/datasets/r/c2539d1c-8531-4937-9cba-3bd8e9786cc5 . That is a truncated zero at the 0.5% public threshold, not a disclosure that nobody is short: the baseline correctly carries anchor_covered=false / register_read_no_position, so this name has NO positioning anchor and its priced_lean_pct of -0.087 is essentially -0.05 x run_up_20d, which is the free control this stage has to beat rather than an independent rival. There is therefore no squeeze fuel and no informed short flow visible in either direction, and my positive number gets no help from positioning. One adjacent fact from the French register that the short file does not carry: on 2026-07-24 Eximium (controlled by Christian Carro) declared it had passively crossed BELOW 5% on 2026-07-06, holding 2,982,231 shares = 4.99% of capital and voting rights, the crossing caused by an increase in ABC arbitrage's own total share and voting-rights count and not by a sale — 'avoir franchi en baisse, le 6 juillet 2026, les seuils de 5% du capital et des droits de vote de la societe ABC ARBITRAGE et detenir, a cette date et a ce jour, 2 982 231 actions ABC ARBITRAGE representant autant de droits de vote, soit 4,99% du capital et des droits de vote de cette societe' — https://fr.ftp.opendatasoft.com/datadila/INFOFI/307/8888/01/FC307639020_20260724.pdf . A long-standing ~5% holder that is not selling; a passive crossing is not evidence of accumulation and I have sized nothing on it.

findings.finding: The half-year about to be printed will show a Produit d'Activite Courante near EUR50m against EUR36.5m in H1 2025 (+39%) — roughly 72% of the ENTIRE unrevised full-year consensus of EUR69.75m delivered in six months — and the conversion arithmetic that the two covering analysts have not updated since 24 March 2026 is what the print actually tests.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the line that produced the two -8% prints in the baseline. 2026-03-24: FY2025 PAC of EUR59.7m matched only Kepler Cheuvreux's PESSIMISTIC EUR60m case against an optimistic EUR66m, net income EUR25.1m against Kepler's EUR27.8m and EPS EUR0.42 against EUR0.47 — the stock fell 8.19% on the day despite a simultaneously disclosed +40% activity pace. 2024-03-26 fell 8.34% on the same line. The three September half-year prints are much smaller: -0.51% (2023), +1.80% (2024), -1.51% (2025) — and the 2025 one fell even though net income doubled and ROE hit 20.3%. So this line can hurt badly in March and has never paid more than +1.80% in September.
findings.original_quote: ABC Arbitrage indique avoir enregistre au 20 mars, un rythme d'activite s'etablissant 40% au-dessus de sa moyenne mensuelle de 2025, et proche des 10% au-dessus de sa moyenne mensuelle du premier semestre 2025. [translation: ABC Arbitrage states that as at 20 March it recorded an activity pace running 40% above its 2025 monthly average, and close to 10% above its H1 2025 monthly average.] This is the conversion key the English wire never published: it pins the 2025-full-year base against the H1-2025 base, so the company's 1 June statement that the Jan-May monthly pace was 'de plus de 70%' above the 2025 monthly average (EUR59.7m/12 = EUR4.98m -> >EUR8.46m per month) maps to roughly +39% on the H1 2025 monthly rate of EUR6.08m, i.e. an H1 2026 PAC near EUR50m, or >=EUR42.3m even if June 2026 earned nothing at all.
findings.why_not_priced: The +70% itself IS disclosed — it was filed as 'Informations privilegiees' on 2026-06-01 and carried in English and French — so I am NOT claiming an undisclosed fact, and researcher_europe/LESSONS.md is right that a pre-print privileged filing means most of the news is out. What is unpriced is the conversion and the fact that nothing has moved to reflect it. If the market had absorbed it, the two covering analysts would not still be carrying price targets 'last updated on Mar 24, 2026' (stockanalysis/S&P Global), the FY2026 revenue estimate would not still read EUR69.75m — which requires June-December 2026 to run at EUR3.92m/month, 21% BELOW the 2025 average and 54% below the disclosed Jan-May 2026 rate — and the stock would not be at EUR5.25 against EUR5.33 on the morning of the release, nearer its EUR4.87 52-week low than its EUR6.19 high, with a 20-day run-up of +1.74%. A French analyst wrote the same observation into a headline on 2026-09-03: 'nette acceleration de l'activite, mais le titre reste sans reaction'. Coverage is 2 analysts on $276k/day of turnover, the band where nobody is positioned for a confirmed fact. This size is already NET of the two things that break the conversion and broke the March print: approximately 45% of value created is redistributed to staff as variable compensation, and Momentum 2028 adds about EUR3m of incremental investment across full-year 2026 — ABC Bourse makes exactly this objection ('Cette phase de developpement pourrait temporairement limiter la conversion de la hausse d'activite en resultat net'). I have netted it here rather than carrying it as a second, contradictory finding.
findings.independence: The consensus side and the activity side come from different documents. Activity: the issuer's own MAR filing, https://fr.ftp.opendatasoft.com/datadila/INFOFI/MKW/2026/06/FCMKW134999_20260601.pdf (2026-06-01). Bar: https://stockanalysis.com/quote/epa/ABCA/forecast/ . Independent third read that the price has not responded: https://www.abcbourse.com/analyses/abc_arbitrage_nette_acceleration_de_lactivite_mais_le_titre_reste_sans_reaction-7116 (2026-09-03). Note this finding shares the 2026-06-01 release with finding 2 below; they use different sentences of it for different purposes (this one the quantum, that one the market-conditions sentence) and I have sized them so they do not double-count the same money.

findings.finding: The obvious bear read of the H2-to-date pace comment — index VIX at its 2026 low, therefore a repeat of the H2 2025 collapse that got the last September print sold — is probably keyed to the wrong market parameter: the company states the Jan-May surge happened in conditions 'broadly comparable' to the prior year, making it capability rather than weather, and H2 2026 has carried record single-stock dispersion with S&P 500 pairwise correlation in the bottom 1% since 2005.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the decisive line on this name in September. On 2025-09-23 the reported half was outstanding — net income doubled, ROE 20.3%, two EUR0.10 interims declared — and the stock fell 1.51%, because the release flagged that volatility had returned to historically low levels since June and H2 activity was down on H1. Kepler's later summary of that year confirms the mechanism: 'l'annee a ete marquee par un premier semestre tres solide, suivi de conditions de marche moins favorables au second semestre'. Conversely on 2026-03-24 a +40% pace statement was NOT enough to save a print whose P&L missed. So a constructive pace comment is necessary but not sufficient, and a weak one is close to sufficient for a negative day.
findings.original_quote: Les parametres de marche observes au cours des premiers mois de l'exercice 2026 sont globalement comparables a ceux constates sur la meme periode en 2025. [translation: The market parameters observed over the first months of the 2026 financial year are broadly comparable to those seen over the same period in 2025.] ABC Bourse draws the identical inference independently on 2026-09-03: 'Cette acceleration intervient dans un environnement de marche pourtant decrit comme globalement comparable a celui du debut 2025. Elle suggere donc une meilleure exploitation des opportunites par les strategies du groupe plutot qu'un simple effet de contexte.' [translation: This acceleration comes in a market environment nonetheless described as broadly comparable to early 2025. It therefore suggests a better exploitation of opportunities by the group's strategies rather than a simple context effect.]
findings.why_not_priced: The visible, quotable, terminal-level statistic on volatility is the VIX, and it is at its 2026 low — 14.2 on 2026-08-14 and 14.81 at the close on 2026-09-18, down from 21.51 in early June. Anyone previewing this print off the wire copy reaches for that number and reproduces the September-2025 trade. What the VIX does not describe is the environment a relative-value arbitrageur is actually paid in: on 2026-07-09 the Cboe S&P 500 Constituent Volatility Index closed at 49.98 against a VIX of 15.84, an all-time record 34.14-point gap and the 98th percentile for VIXEQ, and as of 2026-08-14 the average 60-day pairwise correlation among S&P 500 constituents sat in the bottom 1% of observations since 2005. Low index vol produced by low correlation and high single-stock vol is the opposite regime, for this business, from the genuinely quiet summer of 2025. If the market had made this distinction the stock would not be flat-to-down through a quarter in which its own disclosed activity pace accelerated from +40% (20 March) to +70% (end May). I am sizing this at less than half of finding 1 because LESSONS.md is explicit that macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the company or a direct counterparty has said it, and no ABC arbitrage document names dispersion; the company statement I quote covers January-May, not July-September.
findings.independence: The dispersion and correlation series are from a source with no relationship to the company: https://www.pennmutualam.com/market-insights-news/blogs/chart-of-the-week/2026-08-20-the-sp-500-index-is-calm-its-stocks-aren-t (2026-08-20). The 'capability not context' reading is reached independently by a French analyst who is not one of the two covering brokers: https://www.abcbourse.com/analyses/abc_arbitrage_nette_acceleration_de_lactivite_mais_le_titre_reste_sans_reaction-7116 (2026-09-03). Shares the 2026-06-01 filing with finding 1, on a different sentence.

findings.finding: The 22 September release is the scheduled venue for the first half-yearly distribution decision under the new semi-annual policy, where an already-announced EUR0.20 December interim has to be reconciled with an H1 EPS near EUR0.36-0.40 and a stated 66% payout ratio — against a consensus 2026 DPS of only EUR0.35 on a stock already yielding 6.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Distribution is the single most reliably price-moving line on this name, and it has cut both ways. The 2025-09-23 half-year release declared two EUR0.10 interims and the stock still fell 1.51%. The 2026-03-24 release cut the total 2025 distribution shape to EUR0.34 with an 81% payout and the stock fell 8.19%. In a EUR314m name held largely for a 6.3-6.5% yield, a distribution that merely meets what was already announced is worth nothing and one that lags is worth several points; the asymmetry here is that a raise has not been contemplated by the unrevised estimates.
findings.original_quote: A compter de 2026, la distribution deviendra semestrielle, et un acompte de 0,20 euro par action est prevu pour decembre 2026. [translation: From 2026 the distribution becomes semi-annual, and an interim of EUR0.20 per share is planned for December 2026.] Set against the policy floor reported in the same article, 'un dividende annuel minimum de 0,30 euro et un taux de distribution de 66%', and against the EUR0.35 2026 DPS still carried in consensus at https://stockanalysis.com/quote/epa/ABCA/forecast/ .
findings.why_not_priced: The EUR0.20 is public, so a bare confirmation is neutral and that is why this is the smallest of the three sizes. What is not in the estimates is the arithmetic that a half earning EUR0.36-0.40 per share makes EUR0.20 a ~52% half-year payout against a stated 66% policy, leaving visible headroom at the very moment the board first exercises the new semi-annual mechanism. If the market were carrying that, the 2026 DPS line in consensus would not still read EUR0.35 — barely above the EUR0.34 paid for 2025 — and the yield would not still be 6.48% on a name whose run-rate earnings are ~39% higher than the year that produced it. The offsetting risk, which is why the low end of my band is negative: the 2025 annual release also signalled an intention to strengthen equity via a dividend-reinvestment option from end-2026, and an income-oriented French retail base can read a scrip option as cash retention rather than as capital-return growth.
findings.independence: The semi-annual switch and the EUR0.20 figure are independently reported by a second French outlet: https://www.boursorama.com/bourse/actualites/abc-arbitrage-voit-son-roe-se-tasser-en-2025-e86346d2a0347c440c3294491559b08d (2026-03-24). The policy floor and payout ratio are in the issuer's own English release, https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/03/24/3260946/0/en/ABC-arbitrage-2025-Results.html . This finding rests on a different document from findings 1 and 2.

outside_window.finding: Price-target and estimate revisions from the two covering brokers (Kepler Cheuvreux, target EUR7.40, and TP ICAP Midcap, target EUR6.60) are both stale — Kepler's dates to 2026-03-24 and TP ICAP's to 2025-04-07 — and a half-year PAC near EUR50m makes an upward revision of the FY2026 EUR69.75m revenue and EUR0.52 EPS lines close to mechanical. Notes typically land in the days after the release, not in the single session this stage scores.

Payment of the first interim under the new semi-annual policy, EUR0.20 per share, scheduled for December 2026 — the amount may be confirmed or revised on 22 September but the cash and any scrip election resolve long after the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: Les Echos, Investir, Boursier.com, Zonebourse and actusnews — the brief and LESSONS.md both record these as 403 to curl and WebFetch. I did not burn calls retrying them; Zonebourse surfaced in search results and was routed around rather than fetched.

GlobeNewswire's French-language page over curl: HTTP/2 INTERNAL_ERROR and then 'empty reply from server' over --http1.1. WebFetch on the identical URL returned the body, which is the 'try the other tool once' rule paying off.
The issuer's English AGM report PDF (ABCA-CP-AG-2026-compte-rendu-assemblee-generale-VEng.pdf) — eu_pdftext.py returned only glyph noise, so no figure from it is used anywhere here.

The six monthly 'droits de vote' declarations from the AMF flux (Jan/Apr/Jun/Jul/Aug/Sep 2026) — the prose extracts cleanly but every numeral is in a subset font that eu_pdftext.py cannot map, so I could NOT recover the month-by-month share count and have made no claim about buyback progress or dilution. The only share-count datum I will stand behind is the 59,782,162 shares in the Eximium threshold declaration, which renders correctly.

AMF regulated-information flux queried for ABC arbitrage (ISIN FR0004040608) for anything filed since 2026-09-05: zero records. No pre-release, no 'avertissement sur resultats', no 'revision des perspectives', no ad-hoc 'information privilegiee' in the seventeen days before the print. The last filing of any kind is the 2026-09-04 voting-rights notice.

AMF 'positions courtes nettes' register: ABC arbitrage is not among the 74 French issuers carrying an open disclosed position as of 2026-09-17, so there is no short position at or above the 0.5% threshold to squeeze and no disclosed seller building or covering into the print.

Threshold-crossing history: only two 'franchissement de seuil' filings for this ISIN in the whole flux back to 2012 (2016-05-19 and 2026-07-24), so there is no visible pattern of stake-building by anyone.
Regional and social angles (plan social, site closures, employment) — not applicable: 108 employees on a single Paris site, and nothing in the regional press.
A dated September 2026 broker preview or estimate revision on ABCA in either language — none found; the most recent third-party analysis of any kind is the ABC Bourse technical note of 2026-09-03.

Any company statement linking its activity to equity dispersion or cross-sectional correlation rather than to index volatility — none exists in the filings I read, which is why finding 2 is sized as a hypothesis.
baseline_tension: What I found cuts mildly AGAINST the baseline's negative lean and is close to orthogonal to the run-up: priced_lean_pct is -0.087 but that number is almost entirely -0.05 x run_up_20d because anchor_covered is false, so there is no genuine positioning signal to disagree with — and the run-up itself (+1.74% over 20 days, -0.19% over 5) is so small that there is nothing to fade in either direction, which is itself the observation the whole thesis rests on.
local_pass_note: Added the conversion key that the English wire never carried and that re-anchors the whole thesis: BFM Bourse's 2026-03-24 report of the company's 20-March pace statement ('40% au-dessus de sa moyenne mensuelle de 2025, et proche des 10% au-dessus de sa moyenne mensuelle du premier semestre 2025'). English sources only ever gave the +70% against the 2025 FULL-YEAR average, which is uninterpretable for a half-year print; this pins it to +39% against the H1 2025 monthly rate and turns a vague 'activity is up a lot' into an H1 2026 PAC estimate near EUR50m against EUR36.5m.

Found the reaction-function evidence that forced expected_move DOWN despite the finding sum going up in the fundamental direction: the same French article shows the 2026-03-24 print fell 8.19% while simultaneously disclosing a +40% activity pace, because net income and EPS came in under Kepler Cheuvreux's EUR27.8m / EUR0.47. That is the single most important thing the local pass produced, and it is the reason a bigger beat does not buy a bigger move here.

Found direct, dated, French-language evidence for why_not_priced that no English source provided: ABC Bourse, 2026-09-03, headlined 'nette acceleration de l'activite, mais le titre reste sans reaction' and wrote that the improvement 'peine encore a se traduire dans le parcours boursier' at EUR5.07. That converted 'the market has not focused on this' from an assertion into a sourced observation three weeks old.

Got the original French of the load-bearing market-conditions sentence ('Les parametres de marche observes au cours des premiers mois de l'exercice 2026 sont globalement comparables a ceux constates sur la meme periode en 2025') and an independent French analyst reaching the capability-not-context inference from it, which strengthened finding 2's evidentiary base even though I later cut its size for a different reason.

Added an explicit counterweight from the French press that I had not sized in English: ABC Bourse's objection that the EUR3m Momentum 2028 spend 'pourrait temporairement limiter la conversion de la hausse d'activite en resultat net'. This is netted inside finding 1 rather than carried separately.

Confirmed the event and the session from primary French records rather than the vendor: the AMF flux shows last year's equivalent release filed at 05:00 UTC (07:00 CEST) and the 1 June 2026 regulated filing states the H1 accounts 'seront publies le 22 septembre 2026'. Also confirmed the 2026-07-24 Eximium 4.99% threshold declaration and that nothing at all has been filed since 2026-09-04 — neither exists in English anywhere I could find.

Net effect on the numbers: the fundamental case got materially better sourced (print_vs_bar held at a well-evidenced +25 rather than a hand-waved +30) while the sizes came DOWN, because the local pass supplied the reaction history that the English pass had only as three bare percentages in the baseline.
lessons_applied: 'A German ad-hoc filed before the print may have pre-released the number... The French analogue is information privilegiee.' This landed squarely on my largest finding and cost it the most. The 1 June +70% disclosure is filed in the AMF flux under exactly that category — it IS a pre-release, in English and French, 113 days out. I rewrote finding 1 so it no longer claims an undisclosed fact and instead claims a disclosed fact the price and the estimates have not absorbed, and cut it from +2.0 to +1.1.

'Two findings that cannot both be true are resolved by you, now' and 'a finding whose own text argues against it'. I was carrying a fourth finding at -0.9 (the EUR3m Momentum spend and the ~45% employee share breaking the conversion) which is the mirror image of finding 1's claim. Two findings arguing opposite sides of one mechanism, both resting partly on the 2026-06-01 release, is one finding. Dropped it and netted it into finding 1's text and size. findings_count 4 -> 3.

'Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the company or a direct counterparty has said it.' Finding 2 leans on the VIX/VIXEQ dispersion series and no ABC arbitrage document names dispersion; the company sentence I quote covers January-May, not July-September. Cut from +1.0 to +0.7 and widened the low end to -1.5.

'anchor_covered false means you have no positioning anchor at all and priced_lean_pct is the run-up, which is also the free control.' Rewrote positioning_check to say this explicitly rather than reporting a zero, and rewrote baseline_tension to say the lean is not an independent rival here. No size changed, but the claim I was implicitly making about being unopposed by positioning is now stated as an absence rather than as support.

'Keep findings inside the exit window' — the window is ONE session for a bmo name. Moved the near-certain broker estimate revisions out of findings entirely and into outside_window at +1.5, where they earn nothing. Under the pre-lessons draft I had let some of that optimism sit inside finding 1's upper band; the band is now +3.5 rather than the +5.0 I had in the English draft.

'The hunter's own caveat has to reach the number' and 'understatement is the hunters' systematic error' pulled in opposite directions and roughly cancelled. The caveat argument won narrowly because this name's own September distribution is so tight (-0.51 / +1.80 / -1.51): expected_move 1.8 -> 1.4, now visibly below the +2.3 finding sum, with the gap and its reason stated in conviction_note. I did NOT cut it further to zero, because the same file warns that sizing on certainty rather than on the name's reaction distribution is the systematic error, and because the French tail is intact with no price limit.
Net: impact_sum 2.6 -> 2.3, findings 4 -> 3, expected_move 1.8 -> 1.4, print_vs_bar unchanged at 25.0 because nothing in the file bears on the fundamental arithmetic.
